_comment: Display text for js/db/Health/Diseases.json, which is regenerated by tools/health/gen_diseases.py and therefore never carries a translation. Health_DiseaseSystem._localize lays this over a private copy of the db, keyed by id; only name, desc and the symptom labels are replaced.

adenovirus.name: Adenovirus
adenovirus.desc: A common respiratory virus spread through droplets and contact. Sore throat, conjunctivitis and fever resemble a cold that lingers longer than usual.

aether-lung.name: Aether Lung
aether-lung.desc: Prolonged inhalation of raw, uncondensed aether crystallizes along the alveoli. The lining glows faintly under strain, and each breath grows shorter than the last.

aids.name: AIDS
aids.desc: Advanced HIV infection in which the immune system has collapsed. Wasting and opportunistic infections take hold once CD4 cell counts fall too low to fight back.

alzheimers.name: Alzheimer's Disease
alzheimers.desc: The most common cause of dementia, marked by progressive loss of neurons. Memory for recent events fails first, followed by language and orientation.

amoebiasis.name: Amoebic Dysentery
amoebiasis.desc: Intestinal infection by Entamoeba histolytica. The amoeba erodes the gut lining, producing cramping and, in severe cases, bloody diarrhea.

anemia.name: Iron-Deficiency Anemia
anemia.desc: A shortage of red blood cells caused by insufficient iron. The blood carries less oxygen, leaving the body pale, weak and easily winded.

anthrax.name: Anthrax
anthrax.desc: Infection by Bacillus anthracis spores, whether through the skin, lungs, or gut. Skin exposure produces a black, painless eschar; inhaled spores bring rapid breathlessness.

anxiety.name: Generalized Anxiety
anxiety.desc: A disorder of excessive, hard-to-control worry that outlasts its trigger. Muscle tension and restlessness accompany dread about ordinary, everyday matters.

arrhythmia.name: Cardiac Arrhythmia
arrhythmia.desc: An irregularity in the heart's electrical rhythm, too fast, too slow, or erratic. Palpitations and fainting spells can signal the heart falling out of sync.

ascariasis.name: Roundworm
ascariasis.desc: Infection by a large intestinal roundworm, acquired by swallowing its eggs. Heavy worm burdens cause abdominal distension and rob the body of nutrition.

aspergillosis.name: Aspergillosis
aspergillosis.desc: A mold infection of the lungs, usually in those with prior lung disease or a weakened immune system. Persistent cough and wheeze as spores colonize the airway.

asphalt-cough.name: Asphalt Cough
asphalt-cough.desc: Occupational asthma triggered by prolonged exposure to airborne irritants on the job. The airways narrow and inflame each time the trigger is encountered.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.desc: Chronic inflammation of the airways that narrows them in response to triggers. Wheezing and shortness of breath come in episodes rather than constantly.

athletes-foot.name: Athlete's Foot
athletes-foot.desc: A fungal infection of the skin between the toes, thriving in warm, damp footwear. Itching, scaling and cracking of the skin.

b12-deficiency.name: B12 Deficiency
b12-deficiency.desc: A shortage of vitamin B12 that impairs red blood cell formation and nerve function. Fatigue and numbness in the extremities develop as deficiency progresses.

babesiosis.name: Babesiosis
babesiosis.desc: A tick-borne parasite that infects red blood cells, similar to malaria. Fever and hemolytic anemia follow the parasite's destruction of infected cells.

bedbugs.name: Bedbugs
bedbugs.desc: Small blood-feeding insects that hide in bedding and feed at night. Their bites raise itchy welts, often in a telltale line, and disrupt sleep.

bells-palsy.name: Bell's Palsy
bells-palsy.desc: Sudden, usually one-sided facial nerve paralysis of unclear cause. The affected side of the face droops, unable to smile, blink or raise an eyebrow.

beriberi.name: Beriberi
beriberi.desc: Thiamine deficiency that disrupts nerve and cardiac function. Nerve damage or fluid retention develop depending on which system fails first.

bipolar.name: Bipolar Disorder
bipolar.desc: A mood disorder cycling between depressive lows and abnormally elevated highs. Manic episodes bring reckless energy; depressive ones bring its collapse.

black-mold.name: Black Mold Sickness
black-mold.desc: Chronic exposure to Stachybotrys spores in damp buildings. Headache, brain fog and cough accumulate the longer exposure continues.

bloom-fungus.name: Corpse Bloom
bloom-fungus.desc: A parasitic fungus that hijacks its host's nervous system before fruiting through the flesh. Infection ends only once the fungus has finished growing.

botulism.name: Botulism
botulism.desc: Paralytic poisoning from Clostridium botulinum toxin. Blurred vision and weakness spread from the face downward as nerve signals are blocked.

brain-eating-amoeba.name: Naegleriasis
brain-eating-amoeba.desc: A rare but almost always fatal infection in which a free-living amoeba travels up the olfactory nerve into the brain after entering through the nose. Headache and loss of smell progress rapidly to hallucination and coma.

brucellosis.name: Brucellosis
brucellosis.desc: A bacterial zoonosis contracted from unpasteurized milk or close animal contact. Fever that rises and falls, drenching sweats and joint pain give it the name undulant fever.

campylobacter.name: Campylobacteriosis
campylobacter.desc: One of the most common bacterial causes of foodborne illness. Cramping and diarrhea, sometimes bloody, follow undercooked poultry or contaminated water.

candidiasis.name: Candidiasis
candidiasis.desc: Overgrowth of Candida yeast, normally held in check by the body's flora. White patches or itching discharge appear at the affected mucous membrane.

celiac.name: Celiac Disease
celiac.desc: An autoimmune reaction to gluten that damages the lining of the small intestine. Bloating and malabsorption follow exposure to wheat, barley or rye.

chagas.name: Chagas Disease
chagas.desc: Infection with Trypanosoma cruzi, transmitted by the bite of a triatomine kissing bug. Acute swelling gives way to slow, silent damage to heart muscle over decades.

chickenpox.name: Chickenpox
chickenpox.desc: Primary infection with varicella-zoster virus. An itchy, blistering rash spreads from the trunk outward, scabbing over within a week or two.

chigoe.name: Chigoe Flea
chigoe.desc: A burrowing flea that embeds itself in the skin, usually of the foot, to feed and swell with eggs. A painful, itchy lesion forms around the buried insect.

chikungunya.name: Chikungunya
chikungunya.desc: A mosquito-borne virus named for the contorted posture it forces on sufferers. Fever and severe, often crippling joint pain follow the bite.

chlamydia.name: Chlamydia
chlamydia.desc: The most common bacterial sexually transmitted infection, often symptomless. Discharge or burning appears weeks after exposure when it does present.

cholera.name: Cholera
cholera.desc: Acute intestinal infection by Vibrio cholerae. Profuse watery diarrhea can cause fatal dehydration within hours if fluids are not replaced.

chronic-lyme.name: Late Disseminated Lyme
chronic-lyme.desc: Lyme disease left untreated until the bacteria disseminate widely. Arthritis, nerve damage and facial palsy develop as the infection reaches joints and nerves.

chrono-ague.name: Chronal Ague
chrono-ague.desc: Exposure to unstable temporal fields causes localized aging inconsistent with elapsed time. Sufferers experience brief slips where perceived time and physical time diverge.

cirrhosis.name: Hepatic Cirrhosis
cirrhosis.desc: Irreversible scarring of the liver from chronic disease. Healthy tissue is replaced by fibrous nodules, and jaundice and fluid buildup follow as function fails.

cjd.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
cjd.desc: A prion disease in which misfolded proteins destroy brain tissue. Rapid dementia, muscle jerks and loss of coordination progress over months to death.

cmv.name: Cytomegalovirus
cmv.desc: A herpesvirus that establishes lifelong latency after infection. Usually silent, it can cause prolonged fatigue and mononucleosis-like illness.

cocoon-blight.name: Cocoon Blight
cocoon-blight.desc: A slow hardening of the outer skin into a chrysalis-like shell. Lethargy deepens as metabolic activity redirects toward the hardening process.

collective-vision.name: Collective Vision
collective-vision.desc: A state of collective effervescence, in which a gathered crowd shares the same intense thought or vision at once. The shared euphoria can leave the group sleepless.

common-cold.name: Common Cold
common-cold.desc: A mild upper respiratory infection, usually rhinovirus. Sneezing, congestion and a sore throat that clear within a week without treatment.

convent-mimicry.name: Convent Mimicry
convent-mimicry.desc: Mass psychogenic illness spreading through a closed community. Symptoms and behaviors pass from person to person with no organic cause behind them.

copd.name: COPD
copd.desc: Progressive lung damage, usually from long-term irritant exposure, that narrows the airways permanently. Breathing grows harder over years, not days.

covid.name: Novel Coronavirus
covid.desc: Respiratory infection from SARS-CoV-2. Fever, dry cough and loss of smell are typical; severity ranges from asymptomatic to acute respiratory distress.

crab-lice.name: Crab Lice
crab-lice.desc: A pubic-hair-dwelling louse spread through close contact. Persistent itching and small blue bite marks appear where the lice have fed.

crimean-congo.name: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever
crimean-congo.desc: A tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever with a high fatality rate in severe cases. Fever and bruising progress to bleeding under the skin within two weeks of exposure.

crohns.name: Crohn's Disease
crohns.desc: A form of inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the digestive tract. Cramping and diarrhea flare as the gut lining becomes inflamed.

cryptococcosis.name: Cryptococcosis
cryptococcosis.desc: A fungal infection that colonizes the lungs before spreading to the brain. Headache and confusion mark meningitis once it reaches the central nervous system.

cryptosporidiosis.name: Cryptosporidiosis
cryptosporidiosis.desc: A waterborne protozoan parasite resistant to standard chlorination. Watery diarrhea follows ingestion of its cysts, particularly from contaminated recreational water.

dancing-plague.name: Dancing Fever
dancing-plague.desc: A documented outbreak of compulsive, involuntary dancing, most likely a form of stress-induced mass hysteria. Dancers continued for days until exhaustion or collapse.

data-rot.name: Data Rot
data-rot.desc: Gradual corruption of stored information through accumulated small failures. Errors compound quietly until retrieval turns to garbage.

dengue.name: Dengue Fever
dengue.desc: A mosquito-borne flavivirus infection. Sudden fever accompanies severe joint and bone pain, earning it the nickname breakbone fever.

depression.name: Clinical Depression
depression.desc: A mood disorder marked by persistent low mood and loss of interest in once-enjoyable activities. Fatigue and disrupted sleep compound the weight of it.

diabetes-1.name: Type 1 Diabetes
diabetes-1.desc: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system destroys the pancreas's insulin-producing cells. Blood sugar rises unchecked without external insulin.

diabetes-2.name: Type 2 Diabetes
diabetes-2.desc: Insulin resistance combined with relative insulin deficiency. Persistent thirst, frequent urination and slow-healing wounds develop as blood sugar stays elevated.

diabetic-neuropathy.name: Diabetic Neuropathy
diabetic-neuropathy.desc: Nerve damage from prolonged high blood sugar, most common in the feet and legs. Numbness progresses until injuries and ulcers go unnoticed.

diphtheria.name: Diphtheria
diphtheria.desc: A Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the throat. A thick gray membrane forms across the airway, choking off breath as the illness progresses.

doppelganger-panic.name: Doppelganger Panic
doppelganger-panic.desc: A delusional misidentification disorder in which familiar people are believed to have been replaced by identical impostors. Paranoia hardens around every familiar face.

dream-plague.name: Dream Plague
dream-plague.desc: A contagious affliction of the sleeping mind, passing nightmare content between sufferers. Waking exhaustion accumulates despite hours spent apparently asleep.

ebola.name: Ebola
ebola.desc: A viral hemorrhagic fever spread through contact with bodily fluids. Fever and muscle pain progress rapidly to bleeding and multi-organ failure.

echinococcosis.name: Hydatid Disease
echinococcosis.desc: Infection by tapeworm larvae that form slow-growing, fluid-filled cysts in the liver or lungs. Symptoms appear only once a cyst grows large enough to press on surrounding tissue.

elephantiasis.name: Lymphatic Filariasis
elephantiasis.desc: Lymphatic filariasis, caused by thread-like parasitic worms lodged in the lymph vessels. Chronic blockage causes gross swelling of the limbs, called elephantiasis.

encephalitis-lethargica.name: Sleeping Sickness of the Brain
encephalitis-lethargica.desc: A rare brain inflammation of uncertain viral origin. Tremor and double vision can progress to a statue-like, unresponsive stillness.

endocarditis.name: Infective Endocarditis
endocarditis.desc: A bacterial infection of the heart's inner lining, usually settling on a valve. Fever and a new heart murmur can precede embolic complications elsewhere in the body.

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy
epilepsy.desc: A tendency toward recurrent seizures caused by bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Episodes range from brief lapses to full convulsions.

fainting-sickness.name: Fainting Sickness
fainting-sickness.desc: A form of mass psychogenic illness in which fainting spells spread through a group. Nausea and dizziness precede each collapse, with no infection to explain it.

familiar-fever.name: Familiar Fever
familiar-fever.desc: A febrile bleed-through from a bonded familiar's instincts into the handler's own body. Hunger and reflexes shift toward the familiar's nature as the fever peaks at night.

fatal-insomnia.name: Fatal Familial Insomnia
fatal-insomnia.desc: A prion disease that destroys the thalamus, the brain's sleep-regulating relay. Sleep becomes impossible as the disease progresses, followed by autonomic collapse.

fifth-disease.name: Slapped Cheek
fifth-disease.desc: A mild parvovirus B19 infection, most recognizable by the bright red rash it leaves on the cheeks. Joint ache can follow in older children and adults.

fleas.name: Flea Infestation
fleas.desc: Small jumping insects that live on the blood of a host. Repeated bites raise itchy welts and leave the skin restless and irritated.

gangrene.name: Gangrene
gangrene.desc: Tissue death from interrupted blood supply, often secondary to infection. Skin darkens and breaks down as the affected area loses circulation.

genital-theft-panic.name: Genital-Stealing Witch Panic
genital-theft-panic.desc: A culture-bound delusional panic centered on the belief that the genitals are shrinking or retracting into the body, spreading through fear and rumor rather than any physical cause.

gerd.name: Chronic GERD
gerd.desc: Chronic backflow of stomach acid into the esophagus. Persistent heartburn and regurgitation can erode the esophageal lining over time.

giardiasis.name: Giardiasis
giardiasis.desc: A protozoan parasite of the small intestine, spread through contaminated water. Bloating and greasy diarrhea follow ingestion of its cysts.

glossolalia-wave.name: Speaking Sickness
glossolalia-wave.desc: Fluid, speech-like vocalization without comprehensible meaning, often arising in a trance-like religious state. It can spread contagiously through a gathered crowd.

goiter.name: Iodine-Deficiency Goiter
goiter.desc: Enlargement of the thyroid gland, most often from insufficient dietary iodine. A visible swelling forms at the neck as the gland struggles to keep up.

gonorrhea.name: Gonorrhea
gonorrhea.desc: A sexually transmitted Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection of the genital tract. Discharge and burning on urination, though infection may be silent.

graves.name: Graves' Disease
graves.desc: An autoimmune disease that overstimulates the thyroid gland. Racing heartbeat and bulging eyes accompany the resulting excess of thyroid hormone.

gray-static.name: Gray Static
gray-static.desc: A neurological condition producing a constant field of flickering static across the visual field. Tinnitus and light sensitivity often ride alongside it.

grimoire-tinnitus.name: Grimoire Tinnitus
grimoire-tinnitus.desc: Persistent ringing left behind by prolonged exposure to spoken incantation. Fragments of recited text intrude on thought and disrupt sleep long after the reading ends.

guinea-worm.name: Guinea Worm
guinea-worm.desc: A parasite acquired by drinking water containing infected copepods. The adult worm migrates beneath the skin for a year before emerging through a burning blister.

hand-foot-mouth.name: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease
hand-foot-mouth.desc: An enterovirus infection common in young children. Fever precedes painful mouth ulcers and blisters on the palms and soles.

hantavirus.name: Hantavirus
hantavirus.desc: A rodent-borne virus inhaled from contaminated dust or droppings. Fever progresses to severe respiratory or renal distress depending on the strain.

hashimoto.name: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
hashimoto.desc: An autoimmune disease that gradually destroys the thyroid gland. Fatigue and weight gain creep in as thyroid hormone output slowly fails.

hepatitis-a.name: Hepatitis A
hepatitis-a.desc: A liver infection from the hepatitis A virus, spread by contaminated food or water. Nausea, fatigue and jaundice appear two to six weeks after exposure.

hepatitis-b.name: Hepatitis B
hepatitis-b.desc: Bloodborne or sexually transmitted liver infection. Many carry it silently; others develop fatigue and jaundice as the liver inflames.

hepatitis-c.name: Hepatitis C
hepatitis-c.desc: A bloodborne liver infection often acquired silently. Chronic cases can progress over years to scarring and liver failure if untreated.

herpes-simplex.name: Herpes Simplex
herpes-simplex.desc: A lifelong viral infection of skin and nerve tissue. Painful, fluid-filled blisters recur at the site of latency, triggered by stress or illness.

histoplasmosis.name: Histoplasmosis
histoplasmosis.desc: A fungal lung infection from inhaling spores in soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings. Cough and fatigue follow exposure, usually resolving without treatment.

hiv.name: HIV
hiv.desc: A retrovirus that infects and depletes CD4 immune cells. Left untreated, progressive immune collapse leaves the body open to opportunistic infection.

hollow-shell.name: The Hollow Shell
hollow-shell.desc: An advanced stage of severance from the self, in which the body persists without its usual signs of presence. No reflection is cast, no shadow falls, and the voice that speaks is not recognizably one's own.

hollowing.name: The Hollowing
hollowing.desc: A slow severance between body and self, of uncertain origin. Sensation and memory fade together as the connection thins, leaving cold, unresponsive skin behind.

hookworm.name: Hookworm
hookworm.desc: Intestinal worms that enter through bare skin and migrate to the gut, where they feed on blood. Chronic infection produces anemia and fatigue.

hpv.name: Human Papillomavirus
hpv.desc: A common sexually transmitted DNA virus. Most infections clear on their own; persistent strains can cause warts or precancerous changes.

hypertension.name: Hypertension
hypertension.desc: Persistently elevated blood pressure in the arteries. It rarely causes symptoms directly but quietly strains the heart, kidneys and blood vessels.

ibs.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
ibs.desc: A functional disorder of the gut with no visible structural cause. Cramping abdominal pain and irregular bowel habits recur over months or years.

influenza.name: Influenza
influenza.desc: An RNA virus infecting the respiratory tract. Onset is abrupt: fever, muscle aches, headache and a dry cough that lingers after the fever breaks.

insomnia-chronic.name: Chronic Insomnia
insomnia-chronic.desc: Persistent difficulty falling or staying asleep despite the opportunity to rest. Daytime fatigue and irritability follow each poorly slept night.

iron-lung-curse.name: Iron Lung Curse
iron-lung-curse.desc: A curse that weighs down the breath as though the lungs were slowly filling with metal. A persistent metallic taste accompanies each labored inhale.

japanese-encephalitis.name: Viral Encephalitis
japanese-encephalitis.desc: A mosquito-borne virus that occasionally crosses into the brain. Most infections pass unnoticed, but the minority that inflame the brain bring seizures and paralysis.

kuru.name: Kuru
kuru.desc: A prion disease once transmitted through ritual consumption of infected brain tissue. Tremors and loss of coordination progress as neurons degenerate.

kwashiorkor.name: Kwashiorkor
kwashiorkor.desc: Severe protein malnutrition despite adequate calories. Swelling from fluid retention and a distended, fatty liver mark advanced cases.

lassa.name: Lassa Fever
lassa.desc: A rodent-borne viral hemorrhagic fever endemic to West Africa. Most infections are silent, but severe cases bring fever, bleeding and permanent hearing loss.

laughing-pox.name: Laughing Pox
laughing-pox.desc: A neurological disorder producing sudden, uncontrollable laughing or crying unrelated to actual mood. Pustules mark the skin where the fever has passed through.

laughter-epidemic.name: Laughter Epidemic
laughter-epidemic.desc: A documented outbreak of mass hysteria marked by episodes of uncontrollable laughter spreading through a community, without any infectious agent involved.

leeches.name: Leech Infestation
leeches.desc: Blood-feeding annelid worms that attach with a sucker and release an anticoagulant as they feed. Bites bleed longer than expected and can itch for days after the worm detaches.

legionnaires.name: Legionnaires' Disease
legionnaires.desc: A form of pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria, often from contaminated water systems. Fever and confusion accompany the lung infection.

leishmaniasis.name: Leishmaniasis
leishmaniasis.desc: A sandfly-borne protozoan infection. Depending on the species involved it produces skin ulcers, or spreads internally with fever and organ swelling.

leprosy.name: Leprosy
leprosy.desc: A slow Mycobacterium leprae infection of skin and peripheral nerves. Numb patches and lesions develop as nerve damage accumulates over years.

ley-necrosis.name: Ley Necrosis
ley-necrosis.desc: Collapse of a personal mana channel under catastrophic overdraw, leaving the surrounding tissue without circulation. Numb sigils and cold blood mark the dead channel's spread.

ley-rot.name: Ley Rot
ley-rot.desc: Chronic overdraw on a personal mana channel, which begins to necrotize under sustained load. Bleeding mana and numbness spread from the channel outward as it fails.

lice.name: Head Lice
lice.desc: Infestation of the scalp by the head louse, spread through direct hair contact. Itching from bites may take weeks to develop on a first exposure.

listeriosis.name: Listeriosis
listeriosis.desc: A foodborne bacterial infection, dangerous chiefly to the immunocompromised, newborns and the elderly. Fever and stiff neck can signal spread to the nervous system.

liver-abscess.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess
liver-abscess.desc: A pus-filled cavity in the liver caused by amoebic infection. Right-sided pain and fever develop as the parasite destroys liver tissue from within.

liver-fluke.name: Liver Fluke
liver-fluke.desc: A flatworm parasite acquired from contaminated water plants, which migrates to the liver's bile ducts. Right-sided pain and jaundice follow as the fluke settles in.

loop-amnesia.name: Loop Amnesia
loop-amnesia.desc: Anterograde amnesia: an inability to form new memories after the triggering event. Long-past memories stay intact even as the present slips away unrecorded.

lupus.name: Lupus
lupus.desc: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissue. Joint pain, fatigue and a characteristic facial rash flare and remit unpredictably.

lycanthropy.name: Lycanthropy
lycanthropy.desc: A rare delusional syndrome in which the sufferer is convinced they can, or have, transformed into an animal. The conviction persists despite no physical change having occurred.

lyme.name: Lyme Disease
lyme.desc: A tick-borne Borrelia infection. A spreading bullseye rash is often the first sign, followed by joint pain and fatigue if untreated.

mad-cow.name: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy
mad-cow.desc: A prion disease of cattle that can cross to humans through contaminated tissue. Abnormal behavior and loss of coordination progress as brain tissue turns spongy.

malaria.name: Malaria
malaria.desc: A Plasmodium parasite carried by Anopheles mosquitoes, cycling through red blood cells. Fever spikes and chills recur on a regular schedule as parasites burst free.

mana-plague.name: Mana Plague
mana-plague.desc: A transmissible corruption of the body's arcane channel, provoking uncontrolled discharge. Fever and involuntary spell misfire follow as the channel loses containment.

mange.name: Sarcoptic Mange
mange.desc: A skin infestation by burrowing mites, more familiar in animals but transmissible to people. Crusted skin, hair loss and relentless itching follow the mites' tunneling.

marburg.name: Marburg Fever
marburg.desc: A viral hemorrhagic fever closely related to Ebola, carried by fruit bats. Sudden fever and collapse progress to uncontrolled bleeding.

measles.name: Measles
measles.desc: A highly contagious paramyxovirus spread by airborne droplets. Fever and conjunctivitis precede a spreading rash roughly two weeks after exposure.

melioidosis.name: Melioidosis
melioidosis.desc: A soil-and-water-borne bacterial infection common in tropical regions. Most exposures pass unnoticed, but symptomatic cases range from skin abscess to fever and pneumonia.

meningitis.name: Bacterial Meningitis
meningitis.desc: Bacterial inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord. High fever, stiff neck and severe headache demand urgent treatment.

migraine.name: Chronic Migraine
migraine.desc: A neurological disorder causing recurring, often one-sided headaches. Nausea and sensitivity to light and sound accompany the worst episodes.

miliary-tuberculosis.name: Miliary Tuberculosis
miliary-tuberculosis.desc: A widely disseminated form of tuberculosis that spreads tiny lesions through the bloodstream to multiple organs. Wasting and fever accompany the failure of whichever organs are seeded.

mirror-sickness.name: Mirror Sickness
mirror-sickness.desc: A dissociative affliction in which one's reflection appears to lag behind actual movement. Sufferers report a growing detachment from their own actions as the delay widens.

monkeypox.name: Monkeypox
monkeypox.desc: A viral disease related to smallpox, spread through close contact. A blistering, crusting rash accompanies fever and swollen lymph nodes, usually resolving within weeks.

mononucleosis.name: Mononucleosis
mononucleosis.desc: Epstein-Barr virus infection, spread through saliva. Fever, sore throat and swollen lymph nodes are accompanied by fatigue that can persist for weeks.

mrsa.name: MRSA
mrsa.desc: A staphylococcal strain resistant to standard beta-lactam antibiotics. Skin abscesses and infections that resist first-line treatment.

ms.name: Multiple Sclerosis
ms.desc: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system strips the insulating myelin from nerve fibers. Numbness, vision loss and fatigue appear as damaged nerves misfire.

mucormycosis.name: Mucormycosis
mucormycosis.desc: An aggressive fungal infection favoring the immunocompromised. It spreads rapidly through sinus and facial tissue, leaving a blackened eschar in its wake.

mumps.name: Mumps
mumps.desc: Viral infection of the salivary glands. Fever and malaise give way to painful swelling of the parotid glands at the jawline.

myiasis.name: Botfly Myiasis
myiasis.desc: Infestation of living tissue by fly larvae, which burrow in and feed as they grow. A moving lump under the skin often marks where a larva has taken hold.

name-theft-panic.name: Name Theft Panic
name-theft-panic.desc: A moral panic in which fear over an unproven threat spreads faster than any evidence for it. Suspicion of stolen identity breeds mutism and dread.

narcolepsy.name: Narcolepsy
narcolepsy.desc: A disorder of the brain's sleep-wake regulation. Sudden daytime sleep attacks and, in some cases, a collapse of muscle tone strike without warning.

night-blindness.name: Vitamin A Deficiency
night-blindness.desc: Vitamin A deficiency that impairs the retina's ability to adapt to low light. Difficulty seeing at dusk is often the first sign, before daytime vision is affected.

nipah.name: Nipah Encephalitis
nipah.desc: A bat-borne virus that can jump to pigs and humans. Fever and headache can progress to fatal brain inflammation.

norovirus.name: Norovirus
norovirus.desc: The leading cause of acute gastroenteritis. Sudden vomiting and watery, non-bloody diarrhea spread easily through contaminated hands and surfaces.

null-syndrome.name: Null Syndrome
null-syndrome.desc: A dissociative disorder in which the self feels detached from its own body and thoughts. The world takes on an unreal, muffled distance.

numbers-compulsion.name: Number Station Compulsion
numbers-compulsion.desc: A fixation on shortwave numbers stations, the cryptic broadcasts once used to relay coded messages. Compulsive transcription and monotone speech follow prolonged listening.

ocd.name: OCD
ocd.desc: A disorder of intrusive, unwanted thoughts relieved only by repeated ritual behavior. The compulsion offers brief relief before the obsession returns.

packet-fever.name: Packet Fever
packet-fever.desc: An obsessive fixation on network congestion and dropped connections. Frustration and restlessness build in step with every stalled packet.

parkinsons.name: Parkinson's Disease
parkinsons.desc: A neurodegenerative disease that depletes dopamine-producing neurons. Tremor, rigidity and slowed movement worsen gradually over years.

pellagra.name: Pellagra
pellagra.desc: Niacin deficiency causing damage across skin, gut and brain. Untreated, it progresses through the classic triad of dermatitis, diarrhea and dementia.

pelvic-inflammatory.name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
pelvic-inflammatory.desc: An ascending bacterial infection of the upper female reproductive tract, often silent at first. Untreated, it can scar the fallopian tubes and cause infertility.

petro-lung.name: Petro Lung
petro-lung.desc: Pneumoconiosis: interstitial lung scarring from years of inhaled fine particulate. Breath grows shorter and shallower long after the exposure that caused it has ended.

phantom-gasser.name: Phantom Gasser Panic
phantom-gasser.desc: A documented panic involving reported gas attacks with no confirmed physical agent. Numb legs and terror spread through a community convinced of an unseen assailant.

phantom-infestation.name: Phantom Infestation
phantom-infestation.desc: A delusional disorder in which the sufferer is convinced their body is infested by parasites that are not actually present. The itch feels real even without a cause.

pinworm.name: Pinworm
pinworm.desc: A small intestinal worm whose females migrate to lay eggs around the anus at night. The resulting itch disrupts sleep and spreads eggs to bedding and hands.

plague.name: Bubonic Plague
plague.desc: Yersinia pestis infection from flea bites. Fever and headache precede swollen, agonizing lymph nodes, or buboes, near the site of infection.

pneumonia.name: Bacterial Pneumonia
pneumonia.desc: Bacterial infection of the alveoli. Fever, productive cough and shortness of breath as the lungs fill with inflammatory fluid.

polio.name: Poliomyelitis
polio.desc: Poliovirus infection of the gut, mostly asymptomatic. In a minority of cases the virus reaches the spinal cord and destroys motor neurons, causing paralysis.

possession.name: Possession
possession.desc: An altered state in which control of speech and movement seems to pass to another presence entirely. The body acts and speaks in ways the sufferer does not recognize as their own.

post-viral-syndrome.name: Post-Viral Syndrome
post-viral-syndrome.desc: A disabling fatigue that persists long after the triggering infection has cleared. Exertion, even mild, brings a marked worsening that can last for days.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
psoriasis.desc: An autoimmune skin disease that accelerates skin cell turnover. Thick, itchy plaques of built-up skin form on the scalp, elbows and knees.

ptsd.name: PTSD
ptsd.desc: A trauma-linked disorder in which the nervous system stays locked in threat mode. Flashbacks and hypervigilance persist long after the danger has passed.

q-fever.name: Q Fever
q-fever.desc: A bacterial infection contracted by inhaling spores shed by infected livestock. Fever and headache can progress to pneumonia in a minority of cases.

rabies.name: Rabies
rabies.desc: A near-universally fatal viral encephalitis transmitted through the bite of an infected animal. Agitation, muscle spasms and hydrophobia mark the terminal stage.

recursion-sickness.name: Recursion Sickness
recursion-sickness.desc: A cognitive strain from following a process that calls back into itself without a clean end. Thought loops on the same unresolved step until it collapses under its own weight.

rheumatic-fever.name: Rheumatic Fever
rheumatic-fever.desc: An inflammatory disease triggered by an untreated strep throat infection. It can inflame the heart, joints, skin and brain weeks after the original infection clears.

rheumatoid.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rheumatoid.desc: An autoimmune disease targeting the joint lining. Symmetric swelling and stiffness, worst after rest, gradually erode joint function.

rickets.name: Rickets
rickets.desc: Vitamin D deficiency in growing bone, leaving it soft and prone to bending. Bone pain and visible deformity develop as the skeleton fails to mineralize.

ringworm.name: Ringworm
ringworm.desc: A dermatophyte fungal infection of the skin, despite the name unrelated to worms. A red, scaly, ring-shaped rash spreads outward from the point of contact.

river-blindness.name: River Blindness
river-blindness.desc: Onchocerca worms, transmitted by blackfly bites, release larvae that migrate through the skin and eyes. Severe itching precedes progressive vision loss.

rotavirus.name: Rotavirus
rotavirus.desc: A highly contagious gut virus common in young children. Profuse watery diarrhea and vomiting can cause dangerous dehydration within days.

rubella.name: Rubella
rubella.desc: A generally mild togavirus infection. Half of cases pass unnoticed; when present, a fine rash and swollen lymph nodes appear about two weeks after exposure.

saints-fire.name: Saint's Fire
saints-fire.desc: Ergot alkaloid poisoning from tainted grain. Burning limb pain and vivid hallucination precede gangrene as blood vessels constrict.

salmonellosis.name: Salmonellosis
salmonellosis.desc: A common foodborne bacterial infection. Cramping, diarrhea and fever follow ingestion of contaminated food, usually resolving within a week.

sars.name: Atypical Pneumonia
sars.desc: A coronavirus respiratory disease first identified in 2002. Dry cough and fever progress to dangerously low blood oxygen in severe cases.

satanic-panic.name: Satanic Panic
satanic-panic.desc: A moral panic built on unsubstantiated accusations, spreading through rumor and recovered-memory suggestion rather than evidence. Paranoia and insomnia follow the accusations.

scabies.name: Scabies
scabies.desc: Skin infestation by the microscopic mite Sarcoptes scabiei, which burrows into the outer layer of skin. Intense itching, worse at night, follows visible burrow tracks.

scarlet-fever.name: Scarlet Fever
scarlet-fever.desc: A Streptococcus pyogenes infection producing an erythrogenic toxin. Sore throat and fever accompany a fine, sandpaper-textured rash.

schistosomiasis.name: Schistosomiasis
schistosomiasis.desc: Infection by parasitic flatworms picked up from freshwater contaminated with snail-borne larvae. Eggs lodged in tissue cause chronic inflammation and blood in the urine.

schizophrenia.name: Schizophrenia
schizophrenia.desc: A disorder of disorganized thought and perception. Hallucinations and delusions develop gradually, typically emerging in young adulthood.

scrapie.name: Scrapie Contact
scrapie.desc: A prion disease of sheep and goats, not known to transmit to humans. Relentless itching and stumbling gait mark its progression in the animals it affects.

scurvy.name: Scurvy
scurvy.desc: Vitamin C deficiency that impairs collagen production throughout the body. Bleeding gums, bruising and joint pain follow weeks without fresh produce.

sepsis.name: Sepsis
sepsis.desc: A dysregulated, body-wide response to infection that damages the body's own tissues. Fever, rapid heart rate and confusion signal organ systems failing in cascade.

shigellosis.name: Shigellosis
shigellosis.desc: A bacterial intestinal infection historically known as dysentery. Bloody diarrhea and cramping follow exposure to very small amounts of the bacteria.

shingles.name: Shingles
shingles.desc: Reactivation of dormant varicella-zoster virus in nerve tissue. A painful, blistering rash erupts in a band on one side of the body.

sigil-blight.name: Sigil Blight
sigil-blight.desc: Degradation of the skin's inscribed warding sigils, causing them to smear and misfire. Wards read incorrectly and itching spreads across the affected palms.

sleeping-sickness.name: African Sleeping Sickness
sleeping-sickness.desc: African trypanosomiasis, spread by the tsetse fly. The parasite eventually crosses into the brain, disrupting the sleep-wake cycle and clouding thought.

sleepwalk-pilgrimage.name: Sleepwalking Pilgrimage
sleepwalk-pilgrimage.desc: A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep sleep occur in different brain regions simultaneously, driving complex behavior without conscious awareness. Groups have been known to walk identical routes together.

smallpox.name: Smallpox
smallpox.desc: An eradicated Orthopoxvirus disease, historically devastating. Fever preceded a rash of fluid-filled pustules that scarred survivors for life.

soul-sickness.name: Soul Sickness
soul-sickness.desc: A wasting of the self at a level deeper than the body, of uncertain mechanism. Grief and attachment fade first, followed by a thinning of one's own shadow and name.

spanish-flu.name: Great Influenza
spanish-flu.desc: A severe H1N1 influenza strain responsible for a global pandemic. Rapid onset of high fever and pulmonary edema turned lips and skin cyanotic.

sporotrichosis.name: Sporotrichosis
sporotrichosis.desc: A fungal infection introduced through a skin puncture, often from handling plants or soil. Firm nodules form along the lymph vessels and later ulcerate.

star-madness.name: Star Madness
star-madness.desc: Prolonged exposure to non-Euclidean cosmic geometry overwhelms the mind's spatial reasoning. Persistent visions and dread follow, often outlasting the exposure itself.

static-communion.name: Static Communion
static-communion.desc: A fixation on electronic voice phenomena, the faint patterns some hear as voices within recorded static. Long sessions of listening leave a carrier hum ringing in the ears.

stone-flesh.name: Stone Flesh
stone-flesh.desc: A curse that gradually mineralizes soft tissue, beginning at the extremities. Skin greys and stiffens as flexibility is traded for a slow, creeping rigidity.

strep-throat.name: Strep Throat
strep-throat.desc: Bacterial pharyngitis from Streptococcus pyogenes. Sudden sore throat, fever and inflamed tonsils, without the cough typical of viral infection.

syphilis.name: Syphilis
syphilis.desc: A staged Treponema pallidum infection. A painless chancre marks the primary stage, followed by rash and, untreated, damage to the nervous system.

tapeworm.name: Tapeworm
tapeworm.desc: A ribbon-like intestinal flatworm acquired from undercooked meat. It absorbs nutrients directly through its body wall, leaving the host hungry despite eating.

tarantism.name: Tarantism
tarantism.desc: A historical form of mass hysteria once blamed on spider bite, marked by frenzied dancing said to sweat the venom out. Sweating and melancholy alternate with the fits.

tertiary-syphilis.name: Tertiary Syphilis
tertiary-syphilis.desc: The late, untreated stage of syphilis, years after the original infection. Gummas, dementia and damage to the heart and spinal cord mark systemic organ involvement.

tetanus.name: Tetanus
tetanus.desc: Toxin from Clostridium tetani, entering through a wound, causes progressive muscle rigidity beginning at the jaw and spreading through the body.

the-quiet.name: The Quiet
the-quiet.desc: A rare cosmic affliction that erodes the sufferer's grasp of language and meaning. Words lose their referents one by one, leaving a flat affect and an empty stare.

ticks.name: Tick Infestation
ticks.desc: Blood-feeding arachnids that attach for extended feedings, swelling as they engorge. Local rash and fatigue can follow, along with any pathogen the tick carries.

tower-vertigo.name: Tower Vertigo
tower-vertigo.desc: A disorder of balance in which the world seems to spin or tilt though nothing has moved. Nausea and unsteady footing follow any sudden turn of the head.

toxoplasmosis.name: Toxoplasmosis
toxoplasmosis.desc: Infection with the Toxoplasma gondii parasite, often from undercooked meat or cat feces. Usually mild, but linked to lasting behavioral change once established in the brain.

trachoma.name: Trachoma
trachoma.desc: A chlamydial eye infection and the world's leading infectious cause of blindness. Repeated infection scars the eyelid, turning the lashes inward against the cornea.

trichinosis.name: Trichinosis
trichinosis.desc: A parasitic roundworm infection from undercooked meat. Larvae migrate into muscle tissue, causing swelling, pain and fever as the body reacts to their presence.

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
tuberculosis.desc: A chronic Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the lungs. A persistent cough, weight loss and night sweats develop as the disease becomes active.

typhoid.name: Typhoid Fever
typhoid.desc: A systemic Salmonella Typhi infection from contaminated food or water. Fever climbs in stepwise fashion over several days, with abdominal pain and rash.

typhus.name: Epidemic Typhus
typhus.desc: A louse-borne Rickettsia infection that spreads fastest through crowded, unhygienic conditions. High fever and stupor follow the onset of a spreading rash.

ulcer.name: Peptic Ulcer
ulcer.desc: An open sore in the stomach or duodenal lining, often linked to bacterial infection or long-term irritant use. Burning pain typically worsens or eases around meals.

valley-fever.name: Valley Fever
valley-fever.desc: Coccidioidomycosis, a fungal lung infection from inhaled desert soil spores. Fever, cough and rash appear in the minority who develop symptoms.

void-touch.name: Void Touch
void-touch.desc: Sustained proximity to a void-adjacent phenomenon leaves extremities numb and hair follicles inert. A pervasive, objectless dread accompanies the physical symptoms.

wendigo-hunger.name: Wendigo Hunger
wendigo-hunger.desc: A curse that inverts the body's hunger signal past any satiety point. Insatiable craving, extremity frostbite and mounting paranoia progress together as the affliction deepens.

west-nile.name: West Nile Virus
west-nile.desc: A mosquito-borne virus. Most infections are silent; a minority develop fever, headache and, rarely, neuroinvasive disease.

whipworm.name: Whipworm
whipworm.desc: A whip-shaped intestinal parasite that embeds its thin end in the gut lining. Heavy infections cause bloody stool, cramping and anemia.

whisper-fever.name: Whisper Fever
whisper-fever.desc: A febrile illness accompanied by auditory hallucination, voices heard just below the threshold of words. Fever rises in step with the intensity of what is heard.

whooping-cough.name: Whooping Cough
whooping-cough.desc: A highly contagious Bordetella pertussis infection. Cold-like symptoms give way to weeks of violent coughing fits ending in a characteristic whoop.

windscreen-pitting.name: Windscreen Pitting Delusion
windscreen-pitting.desc: A documented mass panic in which people began noticing ordinary wear on glass and attributed it to a shared, invisible cause. Obsessive inspection followed the rumor.

yellow-fever.name: Yellow Fever
yellow-fever.desc: A mosquito-borne viral hemorrhagic fever. Fever and muscle aches can progress to jaundice, bleeding and liver failure in severe cases.

zika.name: Zika Virus
zika.desc: A mosquito-borne flavivirus, usually mild. Low fever, joint pain and a fine rash resolve within a week, though infection in pregnancy carries separate risks.

broken-arm.name: Broken Arm
broken-arm.desc: A fractured bone in the arm, immobilized in a splint or cast while it knits. Strength on that side is halved until the bone has healed.

broken-leg.name: Broken Leg
broken-leg.desc: A fractured leg bone, set in a cast to hold the break aligned while it mends. Every step must be taken carefully to avoid disturbing the healing bone.

broken-rib.name: Broken Rib
broken-rib.desc: A crack in one or more ribs, usually from blunt trauma. Breathing deeply, coughing or twisting brings a sharp stab of pain until the bone knits.

concussion.name: Concussion
concussion.desc: A mild traumatic brain injury from a blow to the head. Thinking slows and light or noise becomes unpleasant while the brain recovers.

sprained-ankle.name: Sprained Ankle
sprained-ankle.desc: Torn or overstretched ligaments around the ankle joint. Swelling and instability make the joint protest under weight until the ligaments heal.

dislocated-shoulder.name: Dislocated Shoulder
dislocated-shoulder.desc: The upper arm bone forced out of its shoulder socket. The joint is visibly deformed and useless until it is reduced back into place.

deep-laceration.name: Deep Laceration
deep-laceration.desc: A cut through the skin deep enough to expose underlying tissue. It requires closure and careful cleaning to prevent infection while it heals.

severe-burns.name: Severe Burns
severe-burns.desc: Thermal injury deep enough to damage multiple layers of skin. Fluid loss and infection risk rise sharply with the size and depth of the burn.

frostbite.name: Frostbite
frostbite.desc: Tissue damage from prolonged exposure to freezing temperatures. Ice crystals form within cells as circulation to the extremity shuts down to protect the body's core.

whiplash.name: Whiplash
whiplash.desc: A neck injury from sudden, forceful back-and-forth motion, straining muscles and ligaments beyond their normal range. Pain and stiffness often worsen a day or two after the injury.

spinal-injury.name: Spinal Injury
spinal-injury.desc: Damage to the spinal cord that disrupts the signals passing between brain and body. The severity of impairment depends on where along the cord the damage occurred.

amputation.name: Amputation
amputation.desc: Surgical or traumatic loss of a limb. The body must relearn balance and function around the missing structure.

cataract.name: Cataract
cataract.desc: Clouding of the eye's normally clear lens, usually developing slowly with age. Vision dims and blurs as the lens loses its transparency.

hearing-loss.name: Hearing Loss
hearing-loss.desc: Reduced ability to detect sound, from damage to the inner ear or auditory nerve. It can develop gradually from noise exposure or age, or arrive suddenly from injury.

chronic-back-pain.name: Chronic Back Pain
chronic-back-pain.desc: Persistent pain along the spine, often from degenerated discs or strained muscle and ligament. It flares with certain movements and rarely resolves completely.

arthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
arthritis.desc: Wear-related breakdown of joint cartilage, most common in weight-bearing joints. Pain and stiffness worsen with use and ease with rest.

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis
osteoporosis.desc: Progressive loss of bone density that leaves the skeleton porous and fragile. Fractures can occur from falls, or strain, that would not break healthy bone.

kidney-stones.name: Kidney Stones
kidney-stones.desc: Hard mineral deposits that form in the kidney and can lodge in the urinary tract. Passing one brings waves of severe flank pain until it clears.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.desc: Inflammation of the appendix, usually from a blockage that traps bacteria inside. Pain migrates to the lower right abdomen and worsens quickly, requiring prompt surgery.

hernia.name: Hernia
hernia.desc: Protrusion of internal tissue through a weak point in the surrounding muscle wall. A visible bulge appears, often with a dragging discomfort that worsens with strain.

gout.name: Gout
gout.desc: A form of arthritis caused by uric acid crystals accumulating in a joint. Sudden, intense pain and swelling typically strike the big toe first.

chronic-fatigue.name: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
chronic-fatigue.desc: A disabling exhaustion unrelieved by rest, often triggered by illness or physical exertion. Even light activity can bring on a crash that lasts for days.

phantom-limb.name: Phantom Limb Pain
phantom-limb.desc: Pain felt in a limb that is no longer there, after amputation. The brain's map of the body persists even after the body itself has changed.

scar-tissue.name: Old Battle Scars
scar-tissue.desc: Fibrous tissue laid down to close a wound, replacing the original skin's structure. It is less flexible and less sensitive than the tissue it replaces.

cybernetic-rejection.name: Cybernetic Rejection
cybernetic-rejection.desc: An immune response against implanted prosthetic or cybernetic tissue. Inflammation and pain build around the interface as the body treats it as foreign.

mana-burn-scars.name: Mana-Burn Scars
mana-burn-scars.desc: Permanent tissue damage from an arcane channel that overloaded and discharged through the body. The scarring is inert but marks where the burn passed through.

cursed-brand.name: Cursed Brand
cursed-brand.desc: A mark burned into the skin by a curse, binding some lasting effect to the bearer. It does not fade or heal like an ordinary scar.

solomon-curse.name: Solomon's Curse
solomon-curse.desc: A binding affliction tied to an ancient seal, passed down through contact with what it was meant to contain. Its effects trace directly back to the terms of that original binding.

ui.noRemedy: Nothing in the world treats this.
ui.incurableManaged: incurable, can be held in check
ui.undiagnosedDesc: Something is wrong, and nothing yet says what.
